To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Analyst Assist system can: - capture facts about an application, which are represented in a form that is independent of any particular development method; - transform these captured facts into a functional specification, which is represented in the Jackson method; - provide support for the development of an object-oriented database design.
The Analyst Assist system is an effective requirements specification tool.

the Analyst Assist system provides the following advantages: (i) the analyst is freed from the task of having to learn a new method; (ii) the system is able to support the analyst in the early stages of the development process, where the analyst has the greatest need for support; (iii) the system can be used to provide the analyst with an early view of the system to be developed; (iv) the system can assist in the capture of requirements and in the construction of a requirements model
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a requirements specification support system which is based on an understanding of the analyst's modelling activities.
developing knowledge-based systems to support the requirements analysis process.
the application of knowledge-based techniques to the requirements specification process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Analyst Assist system provides a powerful and effective tool for the analyst to use in capturing the user's requirements and to transform these into a formal specification of a system.
Analyst Assist provides a powerful and flexible tool for the development of functional requirements.
the Analyst Assist environment is a useful tool for supporting the requirements analysis process, and is an effective means of producing a functional specification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Analyst Assist system is a tool which supports the analyst during the process of requirements elicitation, specification, and modelling.
the Analyst Assist system has been developed and tested in an industrial context and has demonstrated its potential to support the requirements analysis process.
we have developed a system which provides support for requirements specification in the early stages of the development life-cycle, and which is based on the principles of cognitive modelling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of knowledge-based paradigmas can provide a useful framework for requirements specification, which is independent of any particular development methodology.

a requirements specification support system that is based on knowledge-based techniques can help to overcome the problems of requirements specification by providing a flexible, knowledge-based environment that is independent of any software engineering method.

it is advantageous for the development of requirements specification support environments to be based on the premise of modelling at the early stage of development independent of particular software engineering methods.
